name: 协作与团队任务
description: Task tree (技能树), team quests and peer reviews. Migrated out of api/modules/collaboration in P4.3b.3, following the economy template. Adopts five pre-existing tables under their legacy names and reads a sixth (student_groups, owned by the not-yet-migrated classroom group surface); reaches students, the enable_task_tree feature flag and the shared point ledger exclusively through classroom.public.

provides._routes_note: The three bases are the legacy ones (/api/task-tree, /api/team-quests, /api/peer-reviews) and are deliberately NOT namespaced under /api/collaboration: the deployed frontend calls them, and the endpoint snapshot counts METHOD+PATH. The manifest validator reports one 'not namespaced' warning per route; that is expected and is why this note exists. Renaming them is a coordinated frontend change, not a relocation.
provides._auth_note: All 16 routes - the matrix's '整族无鉴权' family - now resolve the caller from the kernel request context: 401 `未登录或登录已过期` when anonymous, 403 `无权限执行该操作` when the role is not the matrix's set. Ownership is resolved through classroom.public on every request (a teacher owns the classes whose `teacher_id` is their user id, a student their own row and class, a parent their children's classes), and the reads are filtered rather than merely gated: `GET /api/team-quests` with no `class_id` answers the actor's own classes, `GET /api/team-quests/progress` the actor's own students, and `GET /api/peer-reviews` only the rows the actor is party to (the table has no class column, so the scope is its two student ids). `POST /api/peer-reviews` signs the review with the caller (was `reviewer_id` from the body) and `POST /api/team-quests` signs the quest with the calling teacher, or the class's own teacher for a student (was `teacher_id` from the body). RISK NOTE for the Lead to re-rule: the matrix's family-level `teacher（本班）/student（本人）` on the three `/api/task-tree/teacher` write routes is implemented as 'a student acting on their own class', which means a student of a class can create a node whose `points_reward` they can then complete for themselves through the (also matrix-allowed) student completion route. No student-facing caller exists (`taskTreeApi.createNode/updateNode/deleteNode` are used only by TeacherTaskTreePage), so narrowing those three to teacher-only would close that path without touching a live flow - flagged rather than silently narrowed, because the role column is the specification.

data._adopted_note: All five carry their legacy names because a plugin migration may only create p_collaboration_ tables, and because `SELECT *` rows for task_nodes/team_quests/peer_reviews go straight through to the frontend. Renaming is the coordinated P7 namespace migration tracked by guardrail G10.
data._reads_note: SHARED-TABLE DEBT, reported rather than hidden. collaboration only READS student_groups without owning it - one `LEFT JOIN student_groups g ON g.id = s.group_id` in listGroupProgress (api/modules/collaboration/collaboration.service.ts:268) - while api/modules/classroom/classroom.service.ts is the writer (:688 SELECT, :695 INSERT, :239/:634/:708 aggregates) and api/modules/admin/admin.repository.ts deletes from it (:535). It is therefore NOT adopted: adopting would hand this plugin write ownership of a classroom table, and classroom's group surface would have to adopt the same table when it migrates, which G10 forbids. The correct end state is a classroom.public groups accessor (or student_groups moving into the classroom plugin) plus collaboration reading group names through it; until then this declaration grants exactly the read access the domain needs and nothing more. `assignments` (added P4.3b.14) is read for one reason only: the account-deletion cleanup rule derives the assignment ids that match the teacher (`teacher_id = teacherId OR class_id IN classIds`) and deletes `peer_reviews` by `assignment_id`, exactly as the pre-migration cascade did (admin.repository.ts:217-225, 392-399). It is owned by plugins/assignments, so it is a read here, never a second adoption.
data._schema_note: HOST GAP - RESOLVED by the Lead. api/schema/adoptedTables.ts now creates this plugin's adopted tables (and the student_groups read target, plus students.group_id/last_checkin_date/birthday and peer_reviews.team_quest_id) with DDL byte-compatible with api/db.ts:202-207, 403-422, 613-643 and the addColumnIfNotExists calls at :1015/:1093/:1096/:1099. Before that landed, a fresh kernel-composition database had none of these tables and every route here answered 500 'no such table'; the legacy composition was unaffected because initDb() replays the full boot DDL.
